the HLA-B locus of the human MHC is a strong determinant of the outcome of HIV-1 disease, and that the HLA class I peptide binding groove can be used to explain the observed associations.

the course of HIV infection is associated with HLA-B locus alleles, that the course of infection is influenced by the peptide-binding motifs of HLA molecules, and that the course of the infection is also associated with the HLA-B locus allele frequencies in different ethnic groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic markers that are associated with the outcome of HIV infection.
the identification of the HLA-B locus alleles associated with the CD8 T-cell response syndrome.
the role of HLA-B locus alleles in the pathogenesis of HIV-1 infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of the HLA-B45,-49,-50 alleles in the HLA class I region is associated with the development of a CD8+ lymphocytosis in response to HIV infection, whereas the presence of the allele HLA-B35 is associated with a more rapid progression of HIV infection.
HLA-B35 is a strong predictor for rapid progression to opportunistics, while HLA-B45/49/50 (and probably also HLA-B51) is associated with a slower progression to opportunistics".
the HLA-B locus is the single most important host genetic factor influencing the outcome of HIV-1 disease, but that different HLA-B alleles have opposing effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the structural features of the HLA class I molecule can influence the outcome of HIV-1 disease.
HLA B45, B49 and B50 alleles are associated with a favorable outcome of HIV-1 disease, while HLA B35 allele is associated with an unfavorable outcome.
we have shown that HLA-B locus alleles with a shared peptide binding pocket structure are associated with a distinct host response to HIV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the B pocket structure in HLA-B45,-B49,-B50 contains an easily accessible Lys residue at position 145, suggesting that the B pocket is likely to bind a negatively charged anchor residue at position 2 (P2) or 3 (P3) of a bound peptide.
HLA class I polymorphism is an important factor in determining the outcome of HIV infection.
different HLA-B alleles can have contrasting influences on HIV infection.
